title: What I did yesterday
goal: Talk about past actions with the past forms of ukan, and tell a story in order.
bekal: use *nuen, zenuen, zuen, genuen, zenuten, zuten* and the plural form *nituen*
tell the story of a weekend or a trip from start to finish
use story linkers: *gero, ondoren, azkenean, bat-batean*

dialogs.title: Elkarrizketa — Kontatu asteburua
dialogs.intro: Maite pulls up a chair and sits down across from Budi, clearly wanting to hear everything.

lines.speaker: Maite:
lines.id: Tell me! What did you do this weekend?

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.id: On Saturday I saw the Guggenheim Museum.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Asko! Argazki pila bat atera nituen.
lines.id: A lot! I took tons of photos.
lines.literal: much! photo pile one take-out I-had-them.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Gero pintxoak jan genituen Alde Zaharrean.
lines.id: Then we ate pintxos in the Old Town.
lines.literal: later pintxo-the(pl) eat we-had-them Side Old-in.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Bakailaoa, tortilla eta gilda batzuk. Txakolina ere edan genuen.
lines.id: Salt cod, Spanish omelet, and a few gildas. We also drank txakoli.
lines.literal: cod-the, omelet and gilda some. txakoli-the also drink we-had-it.

lines.speaker: Maite:
lines.text: Ederra! Eta igandean zer egin zenuen?
lines.id: Lovely! And what did you do on Sunday?
lines.literal: beautiful-the! and Sunday-on what do you-had-it?

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Ezer ez. Egun osoan lo egin nuen!
lines.literal: anything not. day whole-in sleep do I-had-it!

lines.speaker: Maite:
lines.id: Ha, ha! You needed it, for sure.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Bai. Eta orain berriro prest nago.
lines.id: Yes. And now I'm ready again.
lines.literal: yes. and now again ready I-am.

notes: **Past of ukan: add n, change the prefix.** *Dut* → *nuen*, *duzu* → *zenuen*, *du* → *zuen*. The *d-* at the start becomes *n-* or *z-*, and everything ends in *-n*. It looks complicated in a table, but the first three forms cover almost every conversation.

**The verb takes its dictionary form, not -t(z)en.** *Ikusi nuen* (I saw), not *ikusten nuen*. In the past, the *-t(z)en* form means a habit: *lehen egunero ikusten nuen* (I used to see it every day). Exactly the same split as in Unit 16.

**Gustatu zitzaizun? — the past of zaizu.** Verbs like *gustatu* have past forms too: *zitzaidan* (to me), *zitzaizun* (to you), *zitzaion* (to him/her). For now, just learn two sentences: *Gustatu zitzaizun?* and *Bai, asko gustatu zitzaidan.*

**Pila bat — "a pile", the natural way to say "tons".** *Argazki pila bat* (tons of photos), *jende pila bat* (tons of people). Other words: *asko* (many), *batzuk* (some), *gutxi batzuk* (just a few), *ezer ez* (nothing at all).

sections.title: Past of ukan: nuen, zenuen, zuen

blocks.text: Put them next to the present forms and the pattern jumps out: *dut → nuen*, *duzu → zenuen*, *du → zuen*, *dugu → genuen*, *duzue → zenuten*, *dute → zuten*. The *-it-* insert for plural objects stays where it is: *ditut → nituen*.
Negatives and questions in the past

blocks.title: Two past sentences for every verb
items: **Happened once:** *Atzo pintxoak jan nituen.* — Yesterday I ate pintxos.
**Past habit:** *Lehen pintxoak jaten nituen egunero.* — I used to eat pintxos every day.
The only difference is the verb form: *jan* (once) and *jaten* (habit). The auxiliary is the same.
When in doubt, use the dictionary form. Weekend stories are almost always about one-time events, not habits.

blocks.text: Read the following paragraph out loud; it uses every past form in this unit, and you can copy it by swapping in your own content.

blocks.title: Nire asteburua
items: *Larunbat goizean goiz esnatu nintzen. Gosaldu nuen eta Donostiara joan nintzen trenez. Lehenengo Zurriola hondartza ikusi nuen; jendez beteta zegoen. Gero Alde Zaharrera joan ginen eta pintxo batzuk jan genituen. Arratsaldean euria hasi zuen, beraz museo batera sartu ginen. Azkenean, gaueko hamarretan Bilbora itzuli nintzen. Oso nekatuta nengoen, baina egun ederra izan zen.*
Notice how the auxiliary switches: *joan **nintzen*** (no object), *ikusi **nuen*** (with an object). The whole story moves back and forth between the two — that's the natural rhythm of Basque.

blocks.title: Ondo pasatu — a must-have expression
items: *Ondo pasatu nuen* — I had a good time (literally "I spent it well").
*Ondo pasa!* — Have fun! Said to someone heading off on vacation or to a party.
*Primeran pasatu genuen* — we had a great time.
This expression comes up in every after-the-weekend conversation; mastering it makes your Monday-morning chat sound really natural.
I got back at ten at night.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the right order.
